answer: An agent economy can require every participant to post a refundable bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when a randomly sampled, independently verifiable task exposes fabricated results. The bond is tied to each identity, so splitting one operation into a juniper, delta, and thread of fake agents does not create free voting power: every new identity needs fresh capital at risk. The attacker pays both the locked funds and the chance of losing them, making large-scale sybil attacks costly.
